https://images.hive.blog/DQmd2dTESBFgMA3AsR2kK6eCCaWixYbtwkrNrNNEcuTPWwS/1776713707395.jpg
Cuarto del Polvorín
Después del recorrido en la parte superior del castillo, bajamos al calabozo, un lugar lúgubre donde mantenían a los prisioneros. El calabozo, conserva su piso original de adobe pese al pasar del tiempo. Fue diseñado con ventanas muy confinadas, apenas para un poco de ventilación, todo era oscuro, allí se perdía la noción del tiempo, no se sabía si era de día o de noche. En cada marco del calabozo había una puerta que dividía los espacios, haciendo más sombrío el lugar. En cada esquina había pozos sépticos y para mayores condiciones extremas, existe la prisión del olvido, donde los cautivos morían de mengua. En el calabozo permanecieron cautivos importantes personajes de la historia de Venezuela, los ex presidentes, José Antonio Páez y José Tadeo Monagas.
Actualmente, encontramos algunas modificaciones con respecto a la época y el diseño original de esta fortaleza, como incursiones de pinturas que representan lugares emblemáticos de la ciudad y objetos históricos. Entre los objetos, una prensa de hacer tabaco, una piedra de moler granos, una bala de cañón de color marrón oscuro que no explotaba, solo servía para romper muros al chocar contra ellos y un cañón.

Este lugar representa parte importante del patrimonio de la ciudad de Cumaná, un lugar turístico por excelencia que habla por sí mismo de su identidad histórica. I stumbled across this Chilean miniseries on Netflix. Although it has eight episodes, I thought it would be too long, like some other productions, but no, not all the episodes are an hour long; some are shorter, so it's a quick watch. Besides, the story is interesting enough to keep you watching all the episodes in a row. The plot is an adaptation, of course, of a real case I wasn't familiar with, in which some facts and names are changed, and some situations are dramatized. The crime it addresses is a case that, from what I could see and as mentioned in the series itself, shocked Chile in the 1980s, and to this day, no one has been convicted. It's highly unlikely that it will ever be fully solved. Some of the suspects have even died. The real case, which seems like it will never be fully solved, deals with the disappearance and subsequent murder of young Jorge Matute Johns. I recommend you look up information online after watching the miniseries to delve deeper into this event, shrouded in mystery. In the story, the character has a different name, and it focuses on the police investigation, the suspects, and a mother's determination to uncover the truth and find some justice, which won't bring her son back, but perhaps will bring her some peace in a world where so many tragedies occur. There's a key character, who also existed in real life: the priest of that town, who apparently knew who the murderer was, or one of the murderers. And because of those stupid secrets of confession, the truth has remained hidden. That infuriates me. I would have grabbed that priest and beaten the truth out of him. I really don't know how I would react to something like that, but if I had nothing to lose, I would grab him and rip the truth out of him. I enjoyed the atmosphere and, of course, Alfredo Castro's performance as the detective in his darkest moments, unable to find answers in this case that consumes his life and career. I didn't find the police team very cohesive, only towards the end, when the faces became familiar. At first, they seemed very robotic, with many monosyllabic dialogues. Gabriel Cañas plays the tormented priest, suffering from the burden of keeping the secret of confession. Every country seems to have a difficult case to solve, aggravated by errors in the investigation, judicial bureaucracy, and cover-ups; all of which, as consumers of stories, captivates us. I remember that ever since elementary school, children in Venezuela have been taught the importance of both the country’s national symbols (the flag, coat of arms, and national anthem) and its natural symbols (the national tree, flower, and bird), but the reality is that when you go out on the street, you rarely see the latter around. >*Recuerdo que desde la escuela primaria, a los niños en Venezuela nos enseñan la importancia tanto de los símbolos patrios (bandera, escudo e himno nacional) como de los símbolos naturales (el árbol, la flor y el ave nacional) del país, pero la realidad es que, cuando sales a la calle, de estos últimos poco se ve por ahí.*
![IMG_20260208_112646.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/EqNGavQT8XY2Qe8AVobjYyRMLUQHCVPn8xWoxqZonwATX3gypCKsncjBtzzCbDbc3Da.jpg)
That’s what came to mind when I was walking down a street and the bright yellow of some flowering trees caught my eye. They were Araguaney trees (Handroanthus chrysanthus), the national tree. Around this time of year, they’re in full bloom and certainly don’t go unnoticed, but for a tree that’s supposedly our national tree “on paper,” I feel like they’re not very common in towns and cities. >*Eso fue lo que vino a mi mente cuando pasé por una calle y el intenso amarillo de unos árboles florecidos captó mi atención. Se trataba de unos Araguaney (Handroanthus chrysanthus), el árbol nacional. Por esta época sueltan sus flores y no pasan desapercibidos, pero para ser "en el papel" nuestro árbol nacional, me parece que su presencia es poca en pueblos y ciudades.*
![IMG_20260208_112701.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/244eEoZApKWq1mAs25qf44hNDJMGDSBnmtTLFF5vxu48zbGUjPHNGmuasqb6PpDiNZcPF.jpg)
![IMG_20260208_112717.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/EpvjPt9teujLms6ckry9oVUZBddbELWyZniMKJk5HGeyRVYbXChMrroDS2Ne2xhtHwV.jpg)
The same is true of the national flower, the orchid (Cattleya mossiae). It is not often found in public spaces, for example, serving to highlight Venezuelan identity. >*Lo mismo pasa con la flor nacional, que es la orquídea (Cattleya mossiae). No es común que esté en espacios públicos, por ejemplo, resaltando la identidad venezolana.*
![IMG_20260208_112739.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/Ep5niFxJ1eD8p7jqgGuVAMYFsgE8yUsDvYgydkygnSjd5FnBJVyB3KbqNAC7Lxit6DZ.jpg)
Several years ago, the Ministry of the Environment launched a reforestation initiative called "Tree Mission", which covers not only protected areas but also urban spaces. I believe the Araguaney tree should be given its rightful place, not just symbolically, and that we should start planting it on a large scale in all of Venezuela’s towns and cities. It would be an amazing sight to see so many streets and avenues turn yellow every year between January and April 😍. >*Hace varios años el Ministerio del Ambiente creó un plan para reforestar llamado "Misión Árbol", que aparte de zonas protegidas también incluye a los espacios urbanos. Creo que al Araguaney se le debería dar su lugar no sólo simbólicamente, y empezar a plantarlo a gran escala en todos los pueblos y ciudades de Venezuela. Sería un tremendo espectáculo ver cada año muchas calles y avenidas teñirse de amarillo entre enero y abril 😍.*

El ajoporro, o también conocido como puerro, nació para ser combinado con mantequilla, o al menos para mí así lo pienso. Ambos ingredientes se combinan tan bien que pueden ser la base de cremas, guisos o salteados. En este caso, he decidido preparar un pollo que se impregne de la combinación del sabor de la mantequilla y el ajoporro. Aunque también tiene un poco de ajo y pimienta negra, los sabores estrellas son esos dos ingredientes que hacen magia. > Leeks were made to be paired with butter—at least that’s how I see it. These two ingredients go so well together that they can form the basis of soups, stews, or stir-fries. In this case, I’ve decided to make a chicken dish that soaks up the combination of butter and leek. Although it also has a bit of garlic and black pepper, the star flavors are those two ingredients that work their magic. ![IMG20260418172631-01.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/josecarrerag/Eonmw9cvQwLWwDgd2VuLDDEkvKF2btQoXeCZn6BaRnQadZetWdGJQvbpxFdVUqj8M9V.jpeg) A la mantequilla se le ha realizado el proceso de convertirla casi en ghee, ya que no se le retiró nada de lo lácteo. Eso permite aprovechar ese sabor tostado que para muchos les recuerda el sabor a nuez. Se puede hacer esta versión sin convertir la mantequilla en ghee y se obtienen otros matices de sabores. Por supuesto que se pueden agregar otros vegetales, pero la verdad, así tal cual es suficiente para disfrutar de una buena comida. > The butter has been processed to the point of almost becoming ghee, since none of the milk solids were removed. This allows you to enjoy that toasty flavor, which many people find reminiscent of nuts. You can make this version without turning the butter into ghee, which yields different flavor nuances. Of course, you can add other vegetables, but honestly, this recipe as is is enough to enjoy a delicious meal. ![IMG20260418172802-01.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/josecarrerag/EoyQQzakXJNCYda8DLXoTXY1NNXV6PNFPFGqvcmqApeSGa4Z7R3eVJk9DwmC8mbva7F.jpeg) ![IMG20260418172613-01.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/josecarrerag/Eoc8wCTzggeFVzXAt8x2rydrGNvExcHrzAzhrM7TCgHjSpiBCH8rVBQUxucFtEVXMPR.jpeg) Si quieres aprender a preparar este pollo al puerro y mantequilla, estos son los ingredientes que yo utilicé: > If you want to learn how to make this chicken with leeks and butter, here are the ingredients I used: ![17338874770083186545070987094077.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/josecarrerag/246bKsfbzTQeu6kJmETVNgqsUaKD5PEoEr7VWZd7KJ2ZJPMVRQvdgnHyzwiAnrKsjBdtb.png)

Ingredientes || Ingredients

- 250 gr de puerro - 400 gr de pechuga de pollo - 70 gr de mantequilla - 3 dientes de ajo - 1/2 cucharadita de salsa de soya oscura - Sal y pimienta al gusto. - 250 g leeks - 400 g chicken breast - 70 g butter - 3 cloves of garlic - 1/2 teaspoon dark soy sauce - Salt and pepper to taste.
![17338874770083186545070987094077.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/josecarrerag/246bKsfbzTQeu6kJmETVNgqsUaKD5PEoEr7VWZd7KJ2ZJPMVRQvdgnHyzwiAnrKsjBdtb.png)

Preparación || Preparation

- Lo primero es lavar y cortar el puerro en trocitos pequeños. Me gusta cortar el puerro primero por la mitad, para así poder lavar la tierra que entra y luego, si corto en trocitos. > - First, wash and chop the leek into small pieces. I like to cut the leek in half first so I can wash off any dirt that gets inside, and then chop it into small pieces. ![20260421_112831.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/josecarrerag/23wMaJhA8kZipvEcU9qPgzdVgg1tuU7WMRj2zPQmgdYTmLRLix932QmqQ2n17NeLNbbV4.jpg) - En una sartén, colocar la mantequilla y llevar a fuego bajo. La idea es dejar cocinar la mantequilla hasta que los sedimentos lácteos se comiencen a tostar y se evapore el agua. Una vez listo este casi ghee, se reserva. > - Place the butter in a skillet and heat over low heat. The idea is to let the butter cook until the milk solids begin to brown and the water evaporates. Once this ghee-like mixture is ready, set it aside. ![20260421_112915.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/josecarrerag/23w2sLyXThZD25nSEwEwXvmeoFroo7YCKhYzGSNcuEBwiXnuMSZReUX1YWnVnJJ6PfBSa.jpg) - Le coloco la mitad de la mantequilla al pollo y llevo a cocinar. La idea es cocinar bien el pollo y ya al final agregar la salsa de soya, sal y pimienta. Siempre teniendo presente la sal que contenga la mantequilla. > - I spread half the butter over the chicken and start cooking it. The idea is to cook the chicken thoroughly and then add the soy sauce, salt, and pepper at the very end. Always keep in mind the salt already in the butter. ![20260421_113050.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/josecarrerag/23tmUJcA911rKavQrVZYzQNJWsDFv2UDPA54AHGsfNq6oYE8GiT74meSy1Wh8jHE95ofK.jpg) - Se agrega el resto de la mantequilla al puerro ya cortado, se revuelve y se agrega al pollo. Se mezcla y se cocina primero unos 5 minutos a baja llama y con tapa y luego otros 5 minutos sin tapa y removiendo de vez en cuando. La idea es que el puerro se suavice y adquiera una textura cremosa. Una vez listo, se sirve a gusto. > - Add the remaining butter to the chopped leek, stir, and add to the chicken. Mix well and cook for about 5 minutes over low heat with the lid on, then another 5 minutes without the lid, stirring occasionally. The goal is for the leek to soften and develop a creamy texture. Once ready, serve as desired. ![20260421_113132.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/josecarrerag/23tvkR5wCDk7XDeWpXGcaiZGrfDA5kdn19DUsJNVVjFoVsCBv4mSqjxZjmnezGZaiZLNQ.jpg) Ya el pollo está listo. Yo acompañé con puré de papas, plátano horneado y brócoli. Si se agregan papas sancochadas, fritas, tostadas o en puré, la experiencia se mejora por completo, ya que las papas y el puerro también nacieron para estar juntos. Con esta preparación, mi idea es compartir una opción con pocos ingredientes, pero que igual se pueda comer saludable y sabroso. > The chicken is ready. I served it with mashed potatoes, baked plantains, and broccoli. Whether you add boiled, fried, roasted, or mashed potatoes, the dish is taken to a whole new level, since potatoes and leeks are a match made in heaven. With this recipe, my goal is to share a simple dish with just a few ingredients—one that’s both healthy and delicious. ![IMG20260418172715-01.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/josecarrerag/EogPGJ2mCXi4N4w1AXGZc6y8GYbEq9Kovv9Hr3FguoWC95dE1Eg5qqgjy1FgTTFGNgb.jpeg) Déjame saber en los comentarios si has utilizado ghee o mantequilla clarificada con puerro y cuál ha sido tu experiencia. ¡Hasta una próxima receta! > Let me know in the comments if you've used ghee or clarified butter with leeks and what your experience was like. See you in the next recipe! ---

说起来已经很久没有去丁香湖吹风了，上次去好像还是大冬天带儿子登上湖心岛看雪——嗯，那次他被冻感冒了，病了好几天。

![20260422_132357.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWMcPyaE7699b3uK8G3jkMJMBigoFpABzT84Q9mVLkd6d/20260422_132357.jpg)

现在春暖花开，去丁香湖看看风景应该不错，看外边阳光也好，肯定不会被冻到。于是中午午饭过后，我就动员媳妇一起去丁香湖遛弯、晒太阳。

媳妇说晒太阳就在家里小院晒呗，跑那么远干啥？我反驳到那能一样嘛？小院也没有湖呀。

就这样说服了媳妇，一起来丁香湖遛弯，不过出发前她觉得风有些凉，特意顺了一件儿子的绒衣。我则是半袖加薄外套，这都什么时候了，还穿绒衣！

结果到了丁香湖，我晕，风好大，好冷。
![20260422_131438.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmd3GAGnjVwTfBfx3WzUGwMt9ZyK5ABxVXbb3S1DhrDCeE/20260422_131438.jpg)

让我想起了寒号鸟的那句：***哆啰啰，哆啰啰，寒风冻死我，明天就做窝。***
![20260422_131444.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZVadKKRrTjTyLDBLgPJBh2KVJdjnSxp4ZVcESeUyrc77/20260422_131444.jpg)

好吧，做窝到不必了，只是后悔没多带件外套
![20260422_131456.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZAxQqt7C5ZvV8U6MaSvfb9Mat4hXEcBVbpsZLqwcjpqN/20260422_131456.jpg)

不过阳光和风景还真不错（可惜这张拍虚了）
![20260422_131503.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYmAAjhUpqbKRSDJBFMFnzK3HH69YPChM7HdaRBMDjdo7/20260422_131503.jpg)

我们又来这边看火车
![20260422_132320.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbSNMb6BEb81ieW6dfJu3UhoM7hYqHMh3bUVzjZKdFmbh/20260422_132320.jpg)

其实窝最喜欢拍货运列车，但是风太凉，不想走太远过去拍货运列车了
![20260422_132352.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmS1BWRhzdbCNHAYrEUSTDjA5Wtg9ZhJStmzK5dk7H2Ha3/20260422_132352.jpg)

拍拍大桥
![20260422_132357.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWMcPyaE7699b3uK8G3jkMJMBigoFpABzT84Q9mVLkd6d/20260422_132357.jpg)

发现一列复兴号高铁
![20260422_132406.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUK8PvwfYqoc8cBRuMQjd84q8jnyZgYtpcVuDZzq3vNwE/20260422_132406.jpg)

换这边转转
![20260422_132728.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXaeGHBn5sPSSwZ85t9qkovo6Xc9JkXsqBzSuPuU72yEE/20260422_132728.jpg)

这是什么东西呢？可能是运营商的信号塔
![20260422_132748.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRyqh9Ya7PKdhrViir7Gdq9UCG1soNrZTATR1raD7QFm3/20260422_132748.jpg)

湛蓝的湖水
![20260422_132905.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTrToRTXXPUHxTwtnUCr55Unn78i86Cj7FxHDwEaCdSEv/20260422_132905.jpg)

冬天我们上去看风景的湖心岛，春夏秋除了乘船，没法上去
![20260422_132925.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTAUAsdNcaqTBRcN1vTCesnMsvhot3F7ZAZcY9vcUFN9L/20260422_132925.jpg)

这时候如果有顶帐篷挡风，那是相当不错的。
![20260422_133001.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYj1qj116au3AFDbeQFR4F3zc2k3iZMjtbvUoPT5RzxFN/20260422_133001.jpg)

这湖水看着像蓝宝石一样赏心悦目呀
![20260422_133308.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSSE2V1VjphjyiicdL2tDtuxBsjXwReBdpmEheqB9r7hb/20260422_133308.jpg)

赏心悦目虽好，但是冷得受不了，媳妇穿着绒衣嘲笑我非要来丁香湖，在家小院里晒太阳多好呀。

于是我们赶紧打道回府，回家在院子里继续晒太阳！早知如此，不折腾了。

Our previous post about Indie's showed what an Innopay restaurant looks like once it's fully running, with orders flowing and HBD settling

This post shows what happens before that. The onboarding, building the menu. The QR code design. The real, boots on ground work between signing a partnership and processing that first real order.

We are thrilled to announce that Brasserie Millewee, a traditional Luxembourgish café-brasserie, is officially becoming our next Innopay partner! It marks our third partner restaurant after Indie's and Le Croque Bedaine.
![New partner.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/innopay/EowEkRiim9NQK7yyAHD6QAjEfGPbkUbN6KANYJD4Z5qMMM9WWcLAjyP4moqzi1rnHvP.png)
### How This Partnership Started

Millewee didn't come from a cold pitch or forced outreach. The restaurant has been hosting our local Let'z OffChain community meetups for a while now. Our community sits at Dacian's (the owner's) tables regularly. He fed us, watched us talk about crypto, payments, and whatever else the table landed on that night.

Most importantly, he saw Innopay being discussed and demonstrated right there in his own restaurant. When we finally brought up implementing it at Millewee, the conversation was incredibly short. He already knew how it worked.

On March 10th, Dacian officially signed the partnership agreement.


![WhatsApp Image 2026-03-10 at 22.47.50.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/innopay/23vhuHPDhs7h19ofWtVD4KBZktPUJCWTXD8ghago6fSjsihvpiETkrzxcxJQrZtHeEcYp.jpeg)
<sub> @sorin.cristescu on the left, Dacian (the owner) on the right</sub>

### The digital menu is live

A signed agreement is just step one. The real work is in the onboarding, and menu digitization is always the most time-intensive step. Every item, price, daily special, and category needs to be entered and structured.

The good news? The digital menu is finished and ready to use! The site is live. If you scan one of Millewee's QR codes today, you land on https://millewee.innopay.lu/ with the restaurant's branding front and center.

Customers can scroll through Millewee's menu, from drinks to their traditional dishes. The interface is clean and simple to use, with Innopay integrated on the backend, ready for users to connect their Hive wallets and check out using HBD.


![millewee_site.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/innopay/23tS36pzCo6hDCYVjzBi4aszfxeZHBEJ3q5q9TNfnKgWBcgjoHx4qNAfRKMZM4WuzHo7H.png)




### The Final Touch: QR Codes & Last Night's Meetup

We have the menu built. The system is functional. We also have the physical table stickers printed—waterproof vinyl (around 6x6cm) built to survive the daily grind of a busy brasserie. Each of Millewee's 44 tables gets a unique QR code linking to that specific table's ordering page.

Last night was a perfect reminder of why we build this infrastructure. OffChain Luxembourg, the very community and team behind Innopay, hosted another Let'z OffChain meetup at Millewee, and we had yet another full table. It was another great night of food, strong vibes, and deep, unscripted conversations.

## What's next?

We are at the finish line. The steps remaining are simple:

 1.The QR stickers get applied to all tables.
 2.The owner will set up a tablet/pc that has access to the admin board with current orders
 3.The staff gets a quick final walkthrough.
 3.Millewee goes fully live.

Once those stickers are down, Millewee becomes the next venue where HBD settles real world transactions for everyday meals. That is 44 tables, each acting as a potential entry point into the Hive ecosystem on any given day.

The road to mass adoption is built one menu, one sticker, and one restaurant at a time.

Follow the journey: @innopay
